tagline: A ranch family’s route to the coast winds through mountain canyons.
intro: Highway 33 crosses the Transverse Ranges at Pine Mountain Summit and follows Matilija Canyon toward Ojai. At Wheeler Gorge, the road winds through three tunnels beside cliffs and a creek strewn with boulders. It holds both State Scenic Highway and National Forest Scenic Byway designations; the Forest Service identifies pleasure driving as a primary reason for its designation. Cliffs, rock formations and riverside vegetation stand close to the road, while the corridor provides access to four congressionally designated wildernesses.

The Reyes family largely mapped the route to reach the coast from their ranch on the Cuyama side of the mountains. Known as the Maricopa Highway, it was intended to carry commerce and tourism between the San Joaquin Valley and southern California. The Forest Service now identifies it as especially popular with motorcyclists.

Heading south from the Santa Barbara County line, the state scenic stretch reaches Wheeler Hot Springs; the national-forest designation runs from Lockwood Valley Road to El Roblar Road at the Ojai end. Along the way are Pine Mountain Ridge’s Douglas fir and ponderosa pine, the vertical walls of Sespe Gorge, and Piedra Blanca’s white sandstone. Bellyache Springs and Wheeler Gorge follow on the descent toward Ojai.

moments.title: Sespe Gorge
moments.text: Vertical rock walls mark this stretch of upper Sespe Creek. The gorge lies several miles downstream from the creek’s headwaters. Rock climbers can often be seen practicing bouldering and rappelling here. At the southern end of the gorge, the Sespe Condor Sanctuary has no public access. North of the sanctuary, trails and campgrounds provide access to Sespe Creek and the surrounding Sespe Wilderness.
moments.notice: Notice the vertical rock faces at Sespe Gorge.

moments.title: Bellyache Springs
moments.text: Bellyache Springs has two naming legends. One tells of thirsty travelers who drank too much when they reached the springs and suffered for it. A Forest Service legend instead has early rangers gathering on horseback to complain about their work.

moments.title: Wheeler Springs
moments.text: Wheeler Blumberg found hot sulphur springs here in 1890 after following a deer he had shot into a ravine. He opened a resort the next year with 14 rental cabins and a swimming pool. The resort closed in 1997. The road’s engineering gives another measure of the canyon: three tunnels and three bridges were needed to build the Maricopa Highway through Wheeler Gorge. Water seeping from cliff faces supports maidenhair fern, mosses and orchids. The Youth Conservation Corps built the Wheeler Gorge Nature Trail in 1979, a three-quarter-mile loop following the North Fork of Matilija Creek.
